newsitem.title: USA: Mitsubishi Motors, EEOC still battling.
newsitem.headline: Mitsubishi Motors, EEOC still battling.

text.p: Mitsubishi Motor Manufacturing of America Inc is still battling the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission over a sexual harassment lawsuit, even though it has reached an accord with protesters on workforce diversity issues, the EEOC said Tuesday.

"That's entirely different from our lawsuit," John Hendrickson, regional attorney at the EEOC's Chicago office, said of the accord. "We're in active litigation. They don't appear to have any interest in settlement."
A Mitsubishi Motor Manufacturing of America spokeswoman would not comment on the EEOC case Tuesday.

That lawsuit was filed April 9 in federal court in Peoria, Illinois, seeking back pay with interest and benefits as well as compensatory and punitive damages that could reach $300,000 each for as many as 700 employees at the company's Normal, Illinois, plant.
The suit alleges that many female employees were subjected to sexual harassment which the company failed to address.

Mitsubishi Motor Manufacturing of America is scheduled to hold a news conference Wednesday in New York with officials from minority and women's groups announcing an accord on the boycott of Mitsubishi products and the company's workforce diversity efforts, according to a release announcing the news conference.
The news conference is set to include civil rights leader Jesse Jackson and Patricia Ireland, president of the National Organization for Women.
Mitsubishi Motor Manufacturing of America is a unit of Mitsubishi Motors Corp.
